newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cobepa outperforms on Generale Bank 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: Cobepa outperforms on Generale Bank 'buy'.

text.p: Shares in Belgian holding company Cobepa outperformed the Brussels Bel-20 index, rising 4.00 percent to 1,690 francs on Monday, on the back of a 'buy' recommendation by Generale Bank, dealers said.

The share was also catching up with those of other holding companies, which in the course of a restructuring of the sector have gradually been shedding the discount at which the shares were trading to net asset value.
Generale Bank said Cobepa lagged the bourse in the past few weeks. "Compared to its net asset value the underperformance is even more striking," it said in a report dated July 25.
"We strongly reiterate our 'buy' recommendation," it said.

Shares in retailer GIB, insurer Aegon and German chemicals group Bayer all did significantly better than the Cobepa share, Generale said, pushing the discount to net asset value up to an estimated 23 percent.
Cobepa has stakes in GIB, Aegon and Bayer.
Based on a dividend discount valuation the share should trade at well over 2,000 francs, implying more than 30 percent potential growth from current levels.
Generale noted the sale of Paribas Bank Belgium in which Cobepa holds a 14.1 percent stake would result in "important" capital gains.
"We believe in the discount (to net asset value) fading. Cobepa is following the trend of GBL and Societe Generale (de Belgique)," analyst Stefan Casteleyn at broker Corluy commented.
After moving in a 1,560 to 1,595 franc band since the beginning of July, Cobepa began rising a week ago from 1,585. With Monday's rise the share has broken above resistance in the 1,670 franc area.
